## Task model

```{=latex}
\vspace{0mm}

\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{T} \coloneqq \left(J,\,S,\,A,\,R_{\mathcal{T}},\,p(s_0),\,p(s_{t+1}|s_t,a_t),\,\varrho\right)
\end{equation*}

\vspace{4mm}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
J                  & Trial and action index set with block-specific horizon $n$      \\[\componentrowsep]
S                  & State space of task stimuli, previous task, and task imbalance  \\[\componentrowsep]
A                  & Action set of task selections with binary Yes/No answers        \\[\componentrowsep]
R_{\mathcal{T}}    & Task reward set of trial completion and response correctness     \\[\componentrowsep]
p(s_0)             & Initial state distribution of the block's first stimulus pair    \\[\componentrowsep]
p(s_{t+1}|s_t,a_t) & State-action conditional state distribution of stimulus updates  \\[\componentrowsep]
\varrho            & Task reward function of task completion and response correctness
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
```

## Task model: trial and action index set $J$

```{=latex}
\vspace{0mm}

\begin{equation*}
J \coloneqq \{0,1,\ldots,n\}
\end{equation*}

\vspace{4mm}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
n                & Observed action count, held constant within a block                \\[\componentrowsep]
t = 0,\ldots,n-1 & Decision stages, at each of which one action is selected            \\[\componentrowsep]
t = n            & Horizon boundary, at which the block's decision sequence ends
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{5mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
The block duration is fixed, so $n$ varies across participants and blocks.\\
The model conditions on $n$ and does not describe the response times behind it.
\end{center}
```

## Task model: state space $S$

```{=latex}
\vspace{0mm}

\begin{gather*}
S \coloneqq S_0 \cup S_+,
\quad
S_0 \coloneqq S^1 \times S^2 \times \{\emptyset\} \times \{0\},
\quad
S_+ \coloneqq S^1 \times S^2 \times T \times B
\\[1mm]
s = \left(\left(s^{1,1},s^{1,2}\right),\left(s^{2,1},s^{2,2}\right),s^3,s^4\right)
\end{gather*}

\vspace{3mm}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
S^j = \{(\kappa_j(i),i) \,|\, i \in I_j\} & Labeled stimulus set of Task $j$, of cardinality $n_j$       \\[\componentrowsep]
s^{j,1} \in \{0,1\}                       & Stimulus label, 1 target (PTD) or rotation only (RMC)        \\[\componentrowsep]
s^{j,2} \in I_j = \mathbb{N}_{n_j}        & Stimulus identifier, $n_1 = 18$ patterns, $n_2 = 8$ pairs    \\[\componentrowsep]
s^3 \in T = \{1,2\}                       & Most recently executed task, $\emptyset$ before the first action \\[\componentrowsep]
s^4 \in B = \{-n,\ldots,n\}               & Task imbalance, positive for a surplus of Task 1 actions     \\[\componentrowsep]
|S| = |S^1||S^2|(1 + |T||B|)              & $18 \cdot 8 \cdot (1 + 2 \cdot 491) = 141{,}552$ for $n = 245$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
```

## Task model: action set $A$

```{=latex}
\vspace{0mm}

\begin{equation*}
A \coloneqq \{1,2\} \times \{0,1\},
\qquad
a = (j,k) \in A
\end{equation*}

\vspace{3mm}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
(1,1)                      & Task 1 (target?) answered Yes                                 \\[\componentrowsep]
(1,0)                      & Task 1 (target?) answered No                                  \\[\componentrowsep]
(2,1)                      & Task 2 (rotation only?) answered Yes                          \\[\componentrowsep]
(2,0)                      & Task 2 (rotation only?) answered No                           \\[\componentrowsep]
A^j = \{j\} \times \{0,1\} & Task-specific action sets, $A = A^1 \cup A^2$ and $A^1 \cap A^2 = \emptyset$ \\[\componentrowsep]
\Delta : A \to \{-1,1\}    & Task imbalance increment, $+1$ on $A^1$ and $-1$ on $A^2$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
```

## Task model: task reward set $R_{\mathcal{T}}$

```{=latex}
\vspace{0mm}

\begin{equation*}
R_{\mathcal{T}} \coloneqq \left\{(1,1,0,0),\,(1,0,0,0),\,(0,0,1,1),\,(0,0,1,0)\right\}
\end{equation*}

\vspace{3mm}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
r^1       & Task 1 trial completed                                      \\[\componentrowsep]
r^2       & Task 1 response correct                                     \\[\componentrowsep]
r^3       & Task 2 trial completed                                      \\[\componentrowsep]
r^4       & Task 2 response correct                                     \\[5mm]
(1,1,0,0) & Task 1 performed, response correct                          \\[\componentrowsep]
(1,0,0,0) & Task 1 performed, response incorrect                        \\[\componentrowsep]
(0,0,1,1) & Task 2 performed, response correct                          \\[\componentrowsep]
(0,0,1,0) & Task 2 performed, response incorrect
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
```

## Task model: initial state distribution $p(s_0)$

```{=latex}
\vspace{0mm}

\begin{equation*}
p(s_0) \coloneqq
\prod_{j = 1}^{2}
\left(\frac{1}{2}
\frac{\ib{s_0^{j,2} \in I_{j,s_0^{j,1}}}}{n_{j,s_0^{j,1}}}\right)
\ib{s_0^3 = \emptyset}\,
\ib{s_0^4 = 0},
\qquad s_0 \in S
\end{equation*}

\vspace{3mm}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
\textstyle\prod_{j=1}^{2}                                     & The two task streams are independent at block onset             \\[\componentrowsep]
\tfrac{1}{2}                                                  & Each stimulus label is uniform on $\{0,1\}$                      \\[\componentrowsep]
\ib{s_0^{j,2} \in I_{j,l}} \big/ n_{j,l}                      & Identifier uniform on $I_{j,l} \coloneqq \{i \in I_j \,|\, \kappa_j(i) = l\}$ \\[\componentrowsep]
n_{1,1} = 3,\; n_{1,0} = 15                                   & PTD targets and non-targets                                      \\[\componentrowsep]
n_{2,1} = n_{2,0} = 4                                         & RMC rotation only and rotation and mirror                        \\[\componentrowsep]
\ib{s_0^3 = \emptyset}\,\ib{s_0^4 = 0}                        & No task executed yet and zero task imbalance, so $p(s_0)$ lives on $S_0$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{4mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
There is no previous stimulus at block onset, so direct-repetition exclusion does not apply here.
\end{center}
```

## Task model: conditional state distribution $p(s_{t+1}|s_t,a_t)$

```{=latex}
\vspace{-2mm}

\begin{equation*}
\small
p(s_{t+1}|s_t, a_t) \coloneqq
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{1}{2}
\dfrac{\ib{s_{t+1}^{j,2} \neq s_t^{j,2}}\ib{s_{t+1}^{j,2} \in I_{j,s_{t+1}^{j,1}}}}
      {n_{j,s_{t+1}^{j,1}} - \ib{s_t^{j,2} \in I_{j,s_{t+1}^{j,1}}}}
& \text{regular update, } |s_t^4| < n \text{ and } a_t \in A^j
\\[3mm]
1 & \text{boundary, } |s_t^4| = n \text{ and } s_{t+1} = s_t
\\[1mm]
0 & \text{else}
\end{cases}
\end{equation*}

\vspace{-2mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
\multicolumn{2}{@{}l@{}}{\emph{Regular update.} For $|s_t^4| < n$ and $a_t \in A^j$, the successor state $s_{t+1}$ has} \\[3mm]
s_{t+1}^{j,1}                     & New label of the selected task, uniform on $\{0,1\}$                 \\[\componentrowsep]
s_{t+1}^{j,2}                     & New identifier, uniform on $I_{j,l} \setminus \{s_t^{j,2}\}$, excluding direct repetition \\[\componentrowsep]
s_{t+1}^{3-j} = s_t^{3-j}         & The stimulus of the unselected task unchanged                        \\[\componentrowsep]
s_{t+1}^{3} = j                   & The previous-task component set to the selected task                 \\[\componentrowsep]
s_{t+1}^{4} = s_t^4 + \Delta(a_t) & Task imbalance shifted by $+1$ on Task 1 and $-1$ on Task 2
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{1mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
\emph{Boundary.} The self-loop is reachable only after the final action.
\end{center}
```

## Task model: task reward function $\varrho$

```{=latex}
\vspace{0mm}

\small
\begin{gather*}
\varrho : S \times A \to R_{\mathcal{T}}
\\[1mm]
(s,(j,k)) \mapsto \varrho(s,(j,k)) \coloneqq
\left(\ib{j = 1},\; \ib{j = 1}\ib{k = s^{1,1}},\; \ib{j = 2},\; \ib{j = 2}\ib{k = s^{2,1}}\right)
\end{gather*}

\vspace{3mm}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
\ib{j = 1}                 & Task 1 trial completed                                        \\[\componentrowsep]
\ib{j = 1}\ib{k = s^{1,1}} & Task 1 response correct, answer $k$ matches label $s^{1,1}$   \\[\componentrowsep]
\ib{j = 2}                 & Task 2 trial completed                                        \\[\componentrowsep]
\ib{j = 2}\ib{k = s^{2,1}} & Task 2 response correct, answer $k$ matches label $s^{2,1}$   \\[\componentrowsep]
p(r_{t+1}|s_t,a_t) = \ib{r_{t+1} = \varrho(s_t,a_t)} & The reward is determined by state and action
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{3mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
Component sums over a block give the completed trials (1, 3) and the correct responses (2, 4) per task.\\
$\varrho$ records performance without costs for task switches or task imbalance.
\end{center}
```

## Agent model A1

```{=latex}
\vspace{0mm}

\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{A}_1 \coloneqq \left(\mathcal{T},\; \mathcal{M}_{\chi},\; D,\; p_{\beta,\sigma}(d_t|s_t)\right)
\end{equation*}

\vspace{4mm}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
\mathcal{T}               & Task model, supplying the state and action spaces and the stimulus labels \\[\componentrowsep]
\mathcal{M}_{\chi}        & Reduced FCDT-MDP, from which the optimal task choices are derived          \\[\componentrowsep]
D = A                     & Decision space, the agent's internal counterpart of the action set        \\[\componentrowsep]
p_{\beta,\sigma}(d_t|s_t) & Conditional decision distribution with imbalance $\beta$ and switching cost $\sigma$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{5mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
Decisions $d_t$ are internal and unobserved. The data model relates them to the recorded responses.
\end{center}
```

## Agent model A1: subjective reward function $\rho_{\beta,\sigma}$

```{=latex}
\vspace{-2mm}

\small
\begin{gather*}
\rho_{\beta,\sigma} : S \times A \to \mathbb{R},
\quad
\rho_{\beta,\sigma}(s,a) \coloneqq \rho(s,a) + \rho_{\beta}(s,a) + \rho_{\sigma}(s,a)
\\[1mm]
\rho_{\beta}(s,a) = -\beta\left|s^4 + \Delta(a)\right|,
\qquad
\rho_{\sigma}(s,a) = -\sigma\,\ib{\left(s^3 = 1 \land a \in A^2\right) \lor \left(s^3 = 2 \land a \in A^1\right)}
\end{gather*}

\vspace{1mm}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
\rho(s,a)          & Accuracy, one if the response matches the label of the selected task \\[\componentrowsep]
\rho_{\beta}(s,a)  & Balance, the cost of the task imbalance reached after the action      \\[\componentrowsep]
\rho_{\sigma}(s,a) & Switching, $-\sigma$ if the selected task differs from $s^3$          \\[\componentrowsep]
\beta \in \mathbb{R}  & Positive $\beta$ penalizes imbalance, negative $\beta$ rewards it  \\[\componentrowsep]
\sigma \ge 0          & Accuracy carries unit weight and sets the scale for $\beta$ and $\sigma$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{3mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
The first action incurs no switching cost, since $s^3 = \emptyset$ in the initial state.
\end{center}
```

## Agent model A1: MDP reduction $\chi$

```{=latex}
\vspace{-1mm}

\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{M}_{\beta,\sigma} \;\longrightarrow\; \mathcal{M}_{\chi},
\qquad
\chi : S \to S_{\chi},
\quad
s \mapsto \chi(s) \coloneqq \left(s^3,s^4\right)
\end{equation*}

\vspace{1mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{6mm}}p{88mm}@{}}
\phi : S_+ \to \{0,1\}^2 \times T \times B
& \emph{Identifiers drop out.} No reward depends on them, and excluding direct
  repetitions changes \emph{which} identifier follows, not the probability $1/2$
  of either next label. \\[3mm]
A_{\chi} = \{1,2\}
& \emph{Incorrect actions drop out.} They share the successor distribution and
  all costs with the correct action, which earns exactly one unit more, and are
  therefore strictly dominated. \\[3mm]
\varphi : S_{\phi} \to T \times B
& \emph{Labels drop out.} Under correct responses accuracy is always one, and
  imbalance and switching depend on $s^3$ and $s^4$ alone.
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{2mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
For $n = 245$ this turns $|S| = 141{,}552$ and $|A| = 4$ into $|S_{\chi}| = 983$ and $|A_{\chi}| = 2$.\\
The labels stay in the task state, where action lifting $\lambda$ still needs them.
\end{center}
```

## Agent model A1: reduced FCDT-MDP $\mathcal{M}_{\chi}$

```{=latex}
\vspace{-2mm}

\small
\begin{gather*}
\mathcal{M}_{\chi} \coloneqq \left(J,\, S_{\chi},\, A_{\chi},\, R_{\chi},\, p_{\chi}(s_0),\, p_{\chi}(s_{t+1}|s_t,a_t),\, \rho_{\chi}\right)
\\[1mm]
\rho_{\chi}(s,a) = 1 - \beta\left|s^4 - (-1)^a\right| - \sigma\,\ib{s^3 \in T \setminus \{a\}}
\end{gather*}

\vspace{1mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
S_{\chi} = \{(\emptyset,0)\} \cup (T \times B) & Reduced states, previous task and task imbalance only        \\[\componentrowsep]
A_{\chi} = \{1,2\}                             & Abstract task actions, $a$ selects the correct response for Task $a$ \\[\componentrowsep]
p_{\chi}(s_0)                                  & Degenerate at the reduced initial state $(\emptyset,0)$       \\[\componentrowsep]
p_{\chi}(s_{t+1}|s_t,a_t)                      & Deterministic, $s_{t+1} = \left(a_t, s_t^4 - (-1)^{a_t}\right)$, with boundary self-loop \\[\componentrowsep]
\rho_{\chi}(s,a)                               & One unit of accuracy, minus the imbalance and switching costs \\[\componentrowsep]
v_t^*(s) = v_{\chi,t}^*(\chi(s))               & Optimal values are preserved for every $s \in S$ and $t \in J$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
```

## Agent model A1: optimal policy and decisions

```{=latex}
\vspace{-2mm}

\small
\begin{gather*}
\delta_{\chi,t}^*(s) \coloneqq \min \argmax_{a \in A_{\chi}} q_{\chi,t}^*(s,a),
\qquad
\delta_t^*(s) \coloneqq \lambda\left(s, \delta_{\chi,t}^*(\chi(s))\right)
\\[1mm]
p_{\beta,\sigma}(d_t|s_t) \coloneqq \ib{d_t = \delta_t^*(s_t)}
\end{gather*}

\vspace{1mm}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
q_{\chi,t}^*              & Optimal action-value function of $\mathcal{M}_{\chi}$, by backward induction over $n$ \\[\componentrowsep]
\min \argmax              & Ties are broken towards Task 1, matching the implementation                          \\[\componentrowsep]
\chi(s) = (s^3,s^4)       & The task state is reduced to previous task and task imbalance                        \\[\componentrowsep]
\lambda(s,j) = (j,s^{j,1})& Action lifting reads the response off the stimulus label of Task $j$                 \\[\componentrowsep]
p_{\beta,\sigma}(d_t|s_t) & Degenerate, so A1 is deterministic given state, stage, $\beta$, and $\sigma$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{3mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
No reward discounting, and zero remaining reward at the horizon boundary $t = n$.
\end{center}
```

## Agent model A0

```{=latex}
\vspace{0mm}

\begin{equation*}
p(d_t|s_t) \coloneqq \frac{1}{|D|} = \frac{1}{4}
\end{equation*}

\vspace{4mm}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
D = A                     & Uniform over the four task-response combinations                     \\[\componentrowsep]
\beta,\sigma              & Absent, A0 is a parameter-free baseline                              \\[\componentrowsep]
s_t                       & Ignored, decisions depend on neither state nor history                \\[\componentrowsep]
\lim_{\tau \to \infty} p_{\beta,\sigma,\tau}(a_t|s_t) = \tfrac{1}{4} & The infinite-temperature limit of the A1 response distribution
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{5mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
A0 describes behavior in which optimal action value differences do not influence responses.
\end{center}
```

## Data model $\mathcal{D}$

```{=latex}
\vspace{-2mm}

\small
\begin{gather*}
\mathcal{D} \coloneqq \left(\mathcal{T},\; \mathcal{A}_1,\; p_{\beta,\sigma,\tau}(a_t|s_t)\right)
\\[1mm]
p_{\beta,\sigma,\tau}(a_t|s_t) \coloneqq
\frac{\exp\left(q_t^*(s_t,a_t;\beta,\sigma)/\tau\right)}
     {\sum_{a \in A} \exp\left(q_t^*(s_t,a;\beta,\sigma)/\tau\right)}
\end{gather*}

\vspace{1mm}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
\mathcal{T}                    & Task model, supplying the experimental dynamics                      \\[\componentrowsep]
\mathcal{A}_1                  & Agent model, supplying the optimal action values                     \\[\componentrowsep]
q_t^*(s,a;\beta,\sigma)        & Optimal action-value function of the unreduced FCDT-MDP              \\[\componentrowsep]
\tau > 0                       & Temperature, small $\tau$ concentrates probability on high values    \\[\componentrowsep]
p_{\beta,\sigma,\tau}(a_t|s_t) & Softmax response distribution over the action set $A$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{3mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
The response depends on the entire action-value function, not only on the agent's selected decision $d_t$.
\end{center}
```

## Agentic behavioral model

```{=latex}
\vspace{-2mm}

\small
\begin{gather*}
\theta \coloneqq (\beta,\sigma,\tau) \in \Theta = \left\{(\beta,\sigma,\tau) \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \sigma \ge 0,\ \tau > 0\right\}
\\[1mm]
p_\theta(a_t,d_t|s_t) \coloneqq p_\theta(a_t|s_t)\,p_{\beta,\sigma}(d_t|s_t)
\end{gather*}

\vspace{1mm}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
\mathcal{T}                              & Task model, experimental dynamics and latent task rewards      \\[\componentrowsep]
\mathcal{A}_1                            & Agent model, latent optimal decisions $d_t$                    \\[\componentrowsep]
\mathcal{D}                              & Data model, observed responses $a_t$                           \\[\componentrowsep]
p_\theta(a_t|s_t,d_t) = p_\theta(a_t|s_t) & Response and decision are conditionally independent given $s_t$ \\[\componentrowsep]
b = 1,\ldots,m                           & Blocks independent given $\theta$, each with its own $s_{b,0}$, $m = 6$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{3mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
Task rewards are latent for the agent, and the agent's decisions are latent for the experimenter.
\end{center}
```

## Agentic behavioral model: joint distribution

```{=latex}
\vspace{-3mm}

\footnotesize
\begin{multline*}
p_\theta\left(\left(s_{b,0:n_b-1},\,d_{b,0:n_b-1},\,a_{b,0:n_b-1},\,r_{b,1:n_b}\right)_{b = 1}^{m}\right) \\
= \prod_{b = 1}^{m} \left(
p(s_{b,0}) \prod_{t = 0}^{n_b-1}
p_{\beta,\sigma}(d_{b,t}|s_{b,t})\,p_\theta(a_{b,t}|s_{b,t})\,p(r_{b,t+1}|s_{b,t},a_{b,t})
\prod_{t = 0}^{n_b-2} p(s_{b,t+1}|s_{b,t},a_{b,t})
\right)
\end{multline*}

\vspace{0mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
p(s_{b,0})                       & Initial state of block $b$, with no state carried across blocks \\[\componentrowsep]
p_{\beta,\sigma}(d_{b,t}|s_{b,t})& Latent optimal decision, from the agent model                    \\[\componentrowsep]
p_\theta(a_{b,t}|s_{b,t})        & Observed response, from the data model                           \\[\componentrowsep]
p(r_{b,t+1}|s_{b,t},a_{b,t})     & Latent task reward, from the task model                          \\[\componentrowsep]
p(s_{b,t+1}|s_{b,t},a_{b,t})     & Task dynamics, running only to $t = n_b - 2$                     \\[\componentrowsep]
n_b                              & Observed action count of block $b$, treated as given
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
```

## Sequential conditional log likelihood

```{=latex}
\vspace{-3mm}

\small
\begin{gather*}
p_\theta\left(a_{b,0:n_b-1} \Vert s_{b,0:n_b-1}, r_{b,1:n_b-1}\right)
\coloneqq \prod_{t = 0}^{n_b-1} p_\theta\left(a_{b,t} \,|\, s_{b,0:t}, a_{b,0:t-1}, r_{b,1:t}\right)
\\[1mm]
L(\theta) \coloneqq \prod_{b = 1}^{m} p_\theta\left(a_{b,0:n_b-1} \Vert s_{b,0:n_b-1}, r_{b,1:n_b-1}\right),
\quad
\ell(\theta) \coloneqq \ln L(\theta),
\quad
\hat{\theta} \in \argmax_{\theta \in \Theta} \ell(\theta)
\end{gather*}

\vspace{0mm}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
\Vert                                       & Sequential conditioning on the observed history within block $b$  \\[\componentrowsep]
s_{b,0:t},\, a_{b,0:t-1},\, r_{b,1:t}        & Current and preceding states, preceding actions and rewards       \\[\componentrowsep]
L : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}_{>0}              & Sequential conditional likelihood, a product over the $m$ blocks  \\[\componentrowsep]
\ell : \Theta \to \mathbb{R}                & Sequential conditional log likelihood                             \\[\componentrowsep]
\hat{\theta}                                & Sequential conditional maximum likelihood estimate of $(\beta,\sigma,\tau)$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{3mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
A causal likelihood in the sense of Ziebart et al.\ (2013), related to the partial likelihood of Cox (1975).
\end{center}
```

## Sequential conditional log likelihood: functional form

```{=latex}
\vspace{-3mm}

\small
\begin{gather*}
\ell(\theta)
= \sum_{b = 1}^{m} \sum_{t = 0}^{n_b-1}
\left(
\frac{q_{b,t}^*(s_{b,t},a_{b,t};\beta,\sigma)}{\tau}
- \ln \sum_{a \in A} \exp\left(\frac{q_{b,t}^*(s_{b,t},a;\beta,\sigma)}{\tau}\right)
\right)
\\[1mm]
\text{since}\quad
p_\theta\left(a_t \,|\, s_{0:t}, a_{0:t-1}, r_{1:t}\right) = p_\theta(a_t|s_t)
\end{gather*}

\vspace{0mm}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{$}r<{$}@{\hspace{\componentcolsep}}l@{}}
q_{b,t}^*(s_{b,t},a_{b,t};\beta,\sigma)/\tau & Scaled optimal value of the observed action                        \\[\componentrowsep]
\ln \sum_{a \in A} \exp(\cdot)              & Log normalizer of the softmax over the action set $A$              \\[\componentrowsep]
q_{b,t}^*                                   & Optimal action-value function for design and horizon of block $b$  \\[\componentrowsep]
d_{b,t}                                     & Latent decisions sum out, as $p_\theta(a_t|s_t,d_t) = p_\theta(a_t|s_t)$ \\[\componentrowsep]
s_{0:t-1},\, a_{0:t-1},\, r_{1:t}            & The history drops out of each factor
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{3mm}

\begin{center}
\footnotesize
Successive summation removes all variables after $a_t$, and the earlier factors cancel in the ratio.
\end{center}
```
